Start with tenant isolation and retrieval quality as separate requirements. Store immutable document versions, page/slide coordinates, extraction quality, tenant ID, and ACL/version metadata. Ingestion runs through a durable queue into malware scanning, OCR/layout extraction, table-aware chunking, embedding, and lexical indexing; failed documents enter a retry/dead-letter workflow. Stable chunk IDs make updates and deletions idempotent.

At query time authenticate the user and resolve current groups. Apply tenant and permission filters inside BOTH lexical and vector retrieval; do not retrieve across tenants and hope the final prompt filters secrets. Fuse authorized candidates with RRF, score(d)=Σ1/(c+rank(d)), rerank a bounded shortlist, and assemble cited context. Recheck authorization before returning source content, including when cached results are used. ACL revocation must invalidate relevant cache entries or make their permission versions stale; fail closed if authorization is unavailable.

For an illustrative sizing estimate, 100 million documents × 10 chunks × 768 dimensions × 2 bytes is 1.536 TB of raw vectors before replicas, indexes, metadata, or document storage. Shard primarily by tenant/placement policy, with large tenants partitioned further. Measure authorized recall@k, grounded answer correctness, permission-leak tests, freshness lag, and p95 latency. Hybrid retrieval improves coverage but increases index synchronization work; an LLM is never the authorization boundary.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** Measure retrieval recall separately from grounded answer correctness. A useful groundedness quantity is supported factual claims divided by checked factual claims, but high groundedness alone can reward evasive answers. Pair it with task completion, citation localization, ACL correctness, and deletion propagation. Budget p95 latency across retrieval, reranking, and generation using measured joint behavior.
